items.prompt: Design a phased fictional coastal livelihoods response. Flooding closes a landing route, workers outside the owner register miss support and a cold-room plan charges unaffordable fees. A nearby conservation zone affects shore harvesters. Use all six courses to compare alternatives and identify who can make the next decision.
items.model_answer: Map activities and dependencies. Track labour and protection access with defined denominators. Connect coastal risk and continuity and test displaced burdens. Recognise shore rights and accessible participation and remedy. Verify recurring costs and effective benefits. Present a conditional choice, staffed fallback, evidence tests and accountable review.

items.prompt: Critique a claim that new shoreline investments prove sustainable and equitable development. Boat sales rose, warnings were sent, a site was designated, money was committed and ten ordinary demonstrations worked. Use all six BLU domains to explain what to measure and when to revise or pause.
items.model_answer: Distinguish earnings, food, work and which groups benefit. Compare effective labour and protection access. Follow alerts to achievable action and examine transferred risk. Test conservation outcomes and fair governance. Separate commitment, recurring funding and delivered benefits. Identify exceptions, decision roles and retest conditions.
